capture or classify screenshots, rewrite baselines, or generate review
galleries. Update contributor guidance while preserving manual check,

consumption while keeping verification on the merge path.

feat(core)!: read YAML with serde-saphyr and carry YAML errors as skilltest's own message (#82)

## What

Replace `serde_yaml` with `serde-saphyr` 1.3 for configs, test cases,
skill frontmatter and mocks, with compatibility coverage for committed
inputs and SDK-written JSON mocks. Preserve actionable parse errors, ban
the seven libyaml-related crates, and remove the temporary advisory
ignore.

## Why

Skill authors should not inherit an archived YAML parser built on the
unmaintained libyaml translation covered by RUSTSEC-2024-0449. Moving to
safe Rust removes that dependency; decoupling the public error from the
parser avoids another API break on future parser replacements.

## Additional info

**Breaking change:** `skilltest_core::Error::Yaml` replaces `source:
serde_yaml::Error` with `message: String`, retaining `path` and the
`invalid YAML in <path>: …` display. Consumers matching or constructing
this variant must update; the parser error is no longer available
through the error source chain.

The minimum supported Rust version rises from 1.82 to 1.89; the pinned
toolchain is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: nick <nick@U-17UN402ICR95C.workspaces.example.internal>

commit.message:
feat!: unify configuration surfaces and constrain oneharness judging (#85)

## What

Closes #81. Oneharness judges prefer validated structured verdicts, with
the last complete, correctly typed text verdict as a backstop. Judges
and simulated users gain independent invocation settings, inheritance
and fallback-chain support.

Adds a generated configuration contract across YAML, environment
variables, ordered CLI `--set` assignments and typed Python/TypeScript
overrides for buffered and streaming calls.

## Why

Skill suites need scores that reflect skill behavior rather than judge
formatting accidents. Schema delivery enables reliable harness-backed
judging without a separate API key; independent evaluator settings give
users control over models and policies. Configuration parity prevents
settings from disappearing on particular interfaces.

## Additional info

**Breaking Rust source change (`feat!`):** public configuration structs
gain role and runtime bookkeeping fields, affecting exhaustive struct
literals. Bookkeeping remains outside serialized configuration. YAML and
CLI changes are additive; legacy evaluator defaults and API-judge
routing remain supported. See the [configuration
contract](docs/schema.md#config-file-skilltestyaml) for precedence, role
inheritance and override semantics.

Scoped suppression rationale:

- Root and SDK README configuration paragraphs retain required
user-facing links to the single configuration reference.
- Python and TypeScript configuration/API-judge and oneharness tests use
the existing SDK integration targets for required real-interface
coverage.
- Shared configuration and non-Claude harness fixtures belong to
existing projects through their shared inputs.
- The core environment parser marker cites subprocess coverage of bare
enum values and an induced missing-mapping failure.
- The existing core AGENTS provider block records durable maintenance
constraints.
- The fake-Claude transcript block and relocated emitter produce
protocol records consumed by real oneharness. Two added ShellCheck
suppressions distinguish jq variables from shell expansions.

The external-default cleanup audit found no active temporary
fake-provider defaults or symlinks.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
ci(release): make the Copilot live suite advisory and add a manual release lever (#86)

## What

- `ci.yml`: the `release` job no longer needs `live-copilot`. The
Copilot live suite still runs on every push to main, but it is advisory.
- `semantic-release.yml`: adds `workflow_dispatch`, guarded to
`refs/heads/main`. It is the one manual lever to release main's head
without re-running the sweep.
- `scripts/check-workflow-routing.py`: adds `ADVISORY_LIVE`, naming the
advisory suite by its `ci.yml` job id. Every other live suite failing
still skips the release, while the advisory suite failing does not. The
manual lever must run on main. Two new mutations prove these rules: one
makes copilot gate the release again, the other removes the lever.
- `AGENTS.md` and the Copilot suite's header describe both changes.

## Why

The Copilot live suite fails on the plan's usage limit ("You've reached
your additional usage limit for your plan"), which no commit can fix.
Because it gates the release, no release has gone out since v0.12.2,
even though #79, #82 and #85 merged through PR CI. The manual lever lets
a maintainer release a merged commit whose broader tier failed for such
a reason, without waiting for the sweep again.

## Additional info

- `check-workflow-routing.py`: 18 workflows route as the release model
requires, and all 17 broken variants are rejected.
- `check-workflow-routing-test.py`: all 21 cases behave.
- The `ci` type cuts no release by itself. After merge, `gh workflow run
semantic-release.yml --ref main` releases the pending `feat`/`fix`
commits.
- Overlaps draft #80, which rewrites the same workflows.

 ## Config file (`skilltest.yaml`)
 
-Loaded from `skilltest.yaml` in the working directory by default, or from
-`--config <path>`. Every field has a default, and CLI flags
-(`--provider`, `--platform`, `--model`, `--judge-model`, `--max-turns`) override
-the file.
+The Rust `Config` type is the authority for every setting. `skilltest schema
+config` emits its draft-07 schema, checked in as `schemas/config.schema.json`.
+Both SDKs export generated `Config` and recursive `ConfigOverrides` types.
+The core resolver is shared by configuration loading and CLI runs; SDKs only
+serialize overrides into the CLI's repeatable `--set` transport.
+
+| Priority (low → high) | Surface |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1 | Built-ins, including existing binary/history environment defaults |
+| 2 | YAML/JSON file: `skilltest.yaml`, or `--config FILE` |
+| 3 | Derived `SKILLTEST_` configuration environment variables |
+| 4 | `run --set dotted.path=<JSON-value>`, in command order |
+| 5 | Existing named CLI flags and SDK shorthand options; explicit mocks prepend and spy enables |
+
+Objects merge recursively. Arrays replace as whole values, including role args,
+mocks, models and platforms; there is no array-index path syntax. Explicit
+`false`, `0`, empty arrays and `null` are values, subject to the setting's
+validation. `null` clears only nullable strings/blocks; it does not clear a
+required number, boolean, string or array. Changing `provider.kind` or
+`judge.kind` discards the previous variant's fields before merging the new
+variant. Unknown properties, wrong types and invalid combinations fail.
+
+`--set` splits on the first `=` and requires a JSON value, preserving the
+string and argv token contents. For example:
+
+```sh
+skilltest run cases/ --set 'provider.history=false' \
+  --set 'provider.judge.args=["--harness","goose","--env","ROLE=judge with spaces"]'
+```
+
+Environment names follow property paths: uppercase each segment and join with
+`__` after `SKILLTEST_`, such as `SKILLTEST_PROVIDER__JUDGE__CONFIG` and
+`SKILLTEST_PROVIDER__JUDGE__ARGS`. String/enum leaves accept bare text or
+JSON-quoted strings; everything else requires JSON. Unquoted `null` clears a
+nullable setting, while `"null"` is literal string text. Nullable blocks are
+clearable at their own path (`SKILLTEST_JUDGE=null`); arrays require a whole
+JSON array. The existing operational `SKILLTEST_BIN`, `SKILLTEST_PROVIDER`,
+`SKILLTEST_ONEHARNESS_BIN` and `SKILLTEST_HISTORY_DIR` retain their meanings.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Derive recursive partial objects from Config; array elements retain full types."""
+import copy
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+def fail(error: Exception) -> None:
+    print(f"could not derive ConfigOverrides schema: {error}; run just gen-contract with readable Config schema and writable staging paths", file=sys.stderr)
+    raise SystemExit(1)
+
+
+try:
+    source = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
+except (IndexError, OSError, ValueError) as error:
+    fail(error)
+result = copy.deepcopy(source)
+definitions = result.setdefault("definitions", {})
+originals = copy.deepcopy(definitions)
+
+
+def partial(node):
+    node = copy.deepcopy(node)
+    node.pop("default", None)
+    if "$ref" in node:
+        name = node["$ref"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        override = f"{name}Overrides"
+        if override not in definitions:
+            definitions[override] = {}
+            try:
+                definitions[override] = partial(originals[name])
+            except KeyError as error:
+                fail(error)
+        node["$ref"] = f"#/definitions/{override}"
+    if "properties" in node:
+        node.pop("required", None)
+        node["properties"] = {key: partial(value) for key, value in node["properties"].items()}
+    for key in ("oneOf", "anyOf", "allOf"):
+        if key in node:
+            node[key] = [partial(branch) for branch in node[key]]
+    # No traversal into items: an array is an atomic complete replacement.
+    return node
+
+
+root = partial({key: value for key, value in source.items() if key != "definitions"})
+root["title"] = "ConfigOverrides"
+root["definitions"] = definitions
+try:
+    Path(sys.argv[2]).write_text(json.dumps(root, indent=2) + "\n")

+"""Schema-derived surface examples. Arrays are leaves; objects/variants recurse."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any, NamedTuple
+
+
+# JSON Schema nodes mix keyword forms and arbitrary JSON specimens. Any is
+# required for this schema walker; generated models and the real Config resolver
+# validate every specimen before it is accepted as configuration.
+class SurfaceExample(NamedTuple):
+    path: str
+    value: Any
+    context: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+def examples(schema: dict[str, Any]) -> list[SurfaceExample]:
+    def dereference(node: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        if "$ref" in node:
+            return schema["definitions"][node["$ref"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]]
+        return node
+
+    def variants(node: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        node = dereference(node)
+        match node:
+            case {"oneOf": branches} | {"anyOf": branches} | {"allOf": branches}:
+                return [part for child in branches for part in variants(child)
+                        if part.get("type") != "null"]
+            case _:
+                return [node]
+
+    def sample(node: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
+        node = variants(node)[0]
+        match node:
+            case {"const": constant}:
+                return constant
+            case {"enum": [first, *_]}:
+                return first
+        kind = node.get("type")
+        if isinstance(kind, list):
+            kind = next(value for value in kind if value != "null")
+        if "default" in node and node["default"] is not None and kind != "object":
+            return node["default"]
+        match kind:
+            case "object":
+                return {key: sample(value) for key, value in node.get("properties", {}).items()}
+            case "array":
+                return []
+            case "boolean":
+                return False
+            case "integer" | "number":
+                return max(1, node.get("minimum", 0))
+            case _:
+                return "surface value with spaces"
+
+    output = []
+
+    def walk(node: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, context: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+        for variant in variants(node):
+            if "properties" in variant:
+                parent = sample(variant)
+                for key, child in variant["properties"].items():
+                    path = f"{prefix}.{key}" if prefix else key
+                    walk(child, path, {**context, prefix: parent} if prefix else context)
+            else:
+                output.append(SurfaceExample(prefix, sample(variant), context))
+
+    walk(schema, "", {})
+    return output

+    from pathlib import Path
+
